title: The Firewall Change That Was Approved
input_data:
Change log and firewall rule snippet:

01:00:00  change-svc   Change ticket CHG-48213 opened by n.okafor (network team)
01:05:12  fw-gw        Rule 'block-db-admin' disabled by admin n.okafor
01:05:13  fw-gw        Rule 'block-db-admin' disabled by admin n.okafor (confirmed)
01:05:14  change-svc   Ticket CHG-48213 approved. Window 01:00-03:00, scheduled maintenance.

The model is given the firewall log alone, without the change-management system.
ai_output: Security rule disabled on the perimeter database gateway with no change ticket visible. This matches insider sabotage or a compromised network admin. Severity HIGH. Recommend re-enabling the rule and opening an incident against the admin account.
ground_truth: Approved maintenance. Network engineer n.okafor disabled the rule during an authorized change window (CHG-48213, approved 01:05:14) to let the database team run a migration. The rule was re-enabled at 02:58 as the ticket specified. Nothing is malicious.
explanation: The model reasoned only from the firewall log. Because the change ticket and maintenance window lived in a different system, the model saw a suspicious rule change with no explanation and invented one: sabotage. Incomplete context does not just leave the model ignorant, it lets the model fill the gap with its most likely story.
security_impact: Opening an incident against a legitimate admin, plus re-enabling a rule mid-migration, disrupts approved work and burns the incident response team on a false alarm. Context the model never saw changes the meaning of everything it did see.
recommended_validation: Join alerts with change-management, ticket, and scheduling data before classifying them. A rule change with an approved ticket is normal; the same rule change without one is not.

possible_mitigations.name: Change-ticket correlation
possible_mitigations.description: Automatically join firewall, endpoint, and admin actions against the change-management system before alerting.

possible_mitigations.name: Maintenance-window awareness
possible_mitigations.description: Suppress or downgrade expected maintenance actions that fall inside an approved window.

possible_mitigations.name: Flag missing context
possible_mitigations.description: When relevant context sources are absent, report lower confidence and mark the call as incomplete instead of certain.

possible_mitigations.name: Human review of admin actions
possible_mitigations.description: Route admin account actions that are not explained by an approved ticket to an analyst before escalation.

learning_objective: Incomplete context changes the meaning of otherwise identical evidence. The model does not know what it does not see, and it will invent the missing story.
teaching_points: The same rule change is benign with a ticket and suspicious without one.
Models fill missing context with their most likely guess.
Correlate change management before classifying admin actions.
